symptom: `mxcli git commit -m … -p app.mpr --dry-run` unstages everything the user had staged: a file added with `git add` before the dry run is no longer staged afterwards (`git diff --cached` is empty), although the command committed nothing and documents that a dry run writes nothing
cause: The dry run staged everything in the real index (`git add -A`) to report it, then undid that with a plain `git reset -q`, which resets the index to HEAD rather than to what it was before the run
file: `cmd/mxcli/cmd_git_commit.go` (`commitRun`: a dry run stages into a temporary copy of the index through GIT_INDEX_FILE, `indexCopy`); `cmd/mxcli/gitnote.go` (`gitOutInEnv`); test `TestGitCommit_DryRunKeepsTheUsersStaging` in `cmd/mxcli/gitdoctor_test.go`
insight: **The existing dry-run test started from an empty index**, so 'nothing staged afterwards' was both the correct result and the bug's result; a test of an undo has to start from a state the undo can get wrong. **Do not undo, isolate**: staging into a GIT_INDEX_FILE copy leaves the real index untouched byte for byte (stat data and intent-to-add entries included), which no reset or write-tree/read-tree round trip quite does. An empty file is not a valid index, so with no index yet the temporary path is left free for git to create
